name: Tank
notes: Blackground male soloist and writer working Aaliyah-adjacent programming plus explicit slow jams, 2001–2010. The research gives "56–105; ballads 56–87 with the backbeat on 3", and since the ballad band covers most of the sourced catalogue it is the base: 56–87 felt, `halfTime` true, `halftime_3` snare. F♯ major and F♯ minor are named as his home key and are weighted accordingly. Three drum deltas come from the camp grammar: "syncopated 16th kick pairs" (syncopation 0.6, tresillo lean 0.24, secondary anchor `2a`) with "deliberate silence" as a 0.26 `beatSkipProb`; "snare displaced off the grid" as a 5–11 ms push against the parent's 1–4; and "clicky non-hat percussion", which is a hat lane cut to 0.12 fill density and a four-lane perc/woodblock/rim/snap bed at −5 dB. Harmony is "near-static modal beds with a single Rhodes or bell chord, so the falsetto stack does the harmonic work", so the single-chord family leads and `chordDurationBeats` runs to 32. "Tank's signature is layered falsetto used as the pad" is the high melody register with a `sustain_pad`-led counter at −12. The low end is "sub-808 with portamento slides, alternating with the kick rather than stacking on it" — a moving bass part with a 0.46 `glideProb`, so no `drums.bass808` block, which would have silenced it. ⚠ Confidence is medium; the research says the drum grammar is "inherited from the documented camp" rather than name-specific. ⚠ Every velocity and density number and `swing.amount` 0.54 is INFERRED. ⚠ **`chords.impliedByRiff` declared (2026-08-17, harmony variety floor).** The entry says "near-static modal beds with a single Rhodes or bell chord, **so the falsetto stack does the harmonic work**" and "Tank's signature is layered falsetto used as the pad" - which is this flag's exact meaning: no pad states the changes, the lead does. A single chord is therefore the honest chord lane here, and `chords.rs`'s variety floor exempts a model that says so rather than being cleared with a second chord the entry denies. ⚠ Consequence, and it is wanted: `generators::melody` raises this model's `chordToneBias` from the authored 0.76 to the 0.85 floor, which is what "the falsetto stack does the harmonic work" means in notes. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 940/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** `melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.18 to 0.1. The counter's note count is `densityRatio` times the lead's own note count, so a bar the lead leaves empty is a bar the counter has nothing to answer — and one empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one, which is the single thing a seed cannot vary. Measured across this roster the models failing this gate average 0.150 here against 0.030 for the models that pass. ⚠ The value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "near-static modal beds with a single Rhodes or bell chord, so the falsetto stack does the harmonic work; Tank's signature is layered falsetto used as the pad. "Gone" and "Come Over" with Aaliyah (82, 109) mark the shared grammar.", and every claim in it still holds after the change.
